On one hand, relying on tradition can provide a sense of security and guidance, as you mentioned trusting the collective wisdom of rabbis and scholars over your own instincts. This can be especially helpful when faced with difficult or uncertain situations. By drawing on the insights of others, you can tap into a broader perspective and gain a deeper understanding of the issues at hand. On the other hand, relying too heavily on tradition can lead to a sense of disconnection from your own inner voice and personal values. When you're not actively engaging with your own thoughts and feelings, you may feel like you're simply following a set of rules or guidelines without truly considering the implications of your actions. While tradition can provide a framework for decision-making, it's essential to strike a balance between respecting the wisdom of the past and listening to your own inner voice. Ask questions, explore different perspectives, and engage with the complexities of the issue. 4. **Practice self-reflection and introspection**: Regularly take time to reflect on your thoughts, feelings, and values. This can help you develop a stronger sense of self and increase your confidence in making decisions that align with your own inner voice. By striking a balance between tradition and personal reflection, you can maintain a sense of agency and ownership over your decisions while still honoring the wisdom of the past.
